question.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{xy})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{xy})\,j \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{y}}{2\sqrt{x}}\,i+\frac{\sqrt{x}}{2\sqrt{y}}\,j\text{ }\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x={t}^{3}$ and $y=t$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\frac{\sqrt{t}}{2\sqrt{{t}^{3}}}\,i+\frac{\sqrt{{t}^{3}}}{2\sqrt{t}}\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{2t}\,i+\frac{t}{2}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j \\  & =3{t}^{2}\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{1}{2t}\,i+\frac{t}{2}\,j)\cdot (3{t}^{2}\,i+j) \\  & =\frac{3{t}^{2}}{2t}+\frac{t}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}t+\frac{1}{2}t \\  & =2t.\end{aligned}
$$
